title: Social-Lawful Structure: Boundaries Between Norm, Institution, and Enforceable Rule
summary: This paper candidate develops “Social-Lawful Structure: Boundaries Between Norm, Institution, and Enforceable Rule” from material already present in the Lab corpus. Its current claim ceiling is conceptual synthesis unless comparative legal/social evidence supports stronger claims. The current artifact state is materialized thematic component; title is mined paper framing. The next evidence obligation is comparative cases or explicit non-empirical philosophy framing. Prior to promotion, it requires review against jurisprudence, sociology of law, institutional theory, norms and enforcement.

title: When Local Capture Degrades Global Viability: A Toy Model of Representationally Driven Extraction Feedback
summary: This paper candidate develops “When Local Capture Degrades Global Viability: A Toy Model of Representationally Driven Extraction Feedback” from material already present in the Lab corpus. Its current claim ceiling is properties of the constructed toy model only until empirical calibration. The current artifact state is explicit academic model-paper architecture. The next evidence obligation is executable toy model first; empirical calibration optional later stage. Prior to promotion, it requires review against political economy, extraction models, system dynamics, financial fragility, resilience and maintenance economics.
